result.title: What 30,000 Hours of Ego-centric Video Does Not Teach
result.summary: World models offer a promising alternative to physics-based simulators, yet remain far from practical deployment. We ask how far scaling ego-centric human video takes them, using a dataset of 30,000 hours spanning over 1,000 scene types and 14,000 contributors. Rather than relying on opaque downstream metrics, we directly evaluate agent and object-interaction fidelity on a challenging out-of-distribution benchmark. Increasing training data by 100x improves both, but unevenly: the agent is modeled well, while object fidelity remains far lower and improves slowly. We show that the agent gains need not come from data, and a careful visual conditioning design saturates fidelity with a fraction of it, which lets us measure object fidelity on its own and discover its saturation point. We then introduce a supervision scheme that shifts capacity from scene appearance toward object dynamics, improving object fidelity though a substantial gap remains. Finally, our conclusions transfer to downstream humanoid modeling. Overall, our results suggest that scaling ego-centric data brings agent modeling close to its limit while leaving its effects on the world far behind, and that closing this gap will depend on how models are trained, not only on how much data they see.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用3万小时第一人称视频训练世界模型，在分布外基准上直接评估智能体与物体交互的保真度，发现扩大100倍数据对二者提升不均，并提出把建模容量从场景外观转向物体动力学的监督方案。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「精细视觉条件设计使智能体保真度饱和、再以监督把容量从外观转向动力学」的线索，可能可供核查 LVR 中内部状态是否保留实体动力学而非外观细节，以及视觉证据筛选与容量分配问题，但原文对象是视频世界模型，迁移性尚待核查。
